findings.description: The client-side regex /^[A-Za-z0-9]{12}$/ is correct per spec, but if backend accepts codes that violate the spec during issuance (e.g., via direct database insert or migration from older validation), users will be unable to login from mobile despite web working. Verify backend issuance enforces the same constraint or relax client validation to match actual backend acceptance.

findings.issue: Expired token handling requires network round-trip
findings.description: When the app restores a session with an expired JWT, it sets the user as authenticated and attempts navigation to admin dashboard before any API call reveals the token is invalid. First authenticated request returns 401, interceptor clears storage and redirects. Consider decoding JWT client-side and checking exp claim during restoration to fail fast without network call.

findings.issue: AuthContext navigation effect has no dependency on token validity
findings.description: The navigation effect in AuthContext runs when isAuthenticated changes, but isAuthenticated is derived from presence of user and token, not their validity. If token is present but expired/malformed, user appears authenticated until first API call. Add proactive validation or document this behavior as expected.

findings.issue: SecureStore error handling treats all failures as unrecoverable
findings.description: In secureStorage.ts, errors during getToken/getUser log to console but return null, treating retrieval failure the same as absence. In AuthContext restoreSession, any error triggers clearAuth, potentially deleting a valid token due to transient I/O failure. Consider retry logic or more granular error categorization before clearing storage.
